title: Workflows, agents and who owns the control flow

items.stem: Which statement correctly separates a workflow from an agent, when both are built around a language model?

options.text: A workflow calls the model once, while an agent calls the model many times
In a workflow the code sets the order of steps; in an agent the model does
A workflow can use tools and an agent cannot, since agents only write text
A person approves each step of a workflow, while an agent runs by itself

items.stem: A teammate writes this Python function for the makerspace assistant: it calls the model to pull the machine and date out of the student's message, then always calls check_calendar with them, then calls the model to write a reply from the result. Who owns the control flow, and is this an agent?

options.text: The model owns it, because the model is called twice; so it is an agent
The model owns it, because it writes the reply; so it is an agent
The student owns it, because their message starts it; so it is a workflow
The code owns it, because the steps are fixed; so it is a workflow

items.stem: Which part of the makerspace assistant is the best candidate for a fixed workflow rather than an agent?

options.text: Confirming a booking: check the slot is free, reserve it, then email the student, in that order every time
Diagnosing a jammed 3D printer by reading several manuals, with no way to know how many lookups it needs
Answering a vague question such as "what could I build for my project?", where the needed steps are unclear
Helping a student plan a project that may need several machines, with each check depending on the last

items.stem: Your sponsor's budget covers 6,000 model calls for the semester. A fixed workflow answers each request with exactly 2 model calls. An agent version averages 5 model calls per request. How many more requests can the budget cover with the workflow than with the agent?
In one sentence, why does a fixed workflow usually cost less and behave more predictably than an agent doing the same job?
In one sentence, what is the property of a task that makes an agent a better choice than a fixed workflow?
